stem: Which diagnostic tool is best suited to exclude malrotation by ensuring the small bowel is normally positioned?
explanation: A contrast study allows clinicians to visualize the anatomical path of the GI tract and confirm the correct position of the small bowel.
rationale: Consider a radiological procedure that uses a swallowed dye to map the structure of the digestive system.

optionExplanations.A: Endoscopy looks at the internal lining of the esophagus and stomach but is not the standard for assessing overall bowel rotation.
optionExplanations.B: pH studies measure acid levels over time but provide no information regarding the physical anatomy or position of the bowel.
optionExplanations.C: While useful for pyloric stenosis, ultrasound is less definitive than contrast studies for diagnosing malrotation.
optionExplanations.D: A contrast study allows clinicians to visualize the anatomical path of the GI tract and confirm the correct position of the small bowel.

source.hint: Consider a radiological procedure that uses a swallowed dye to map the structure of the digestive system.
